title: Isolation Levels and Anomalies
oneLiner: Dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantoms, lost updates and write skew, which isolation level stops each, and MVCC versus locking.
keyTakeaway: Default isolation (read committed in PostgreSQL and SQL Server, repeatable read in MySQL) does not stop lost updates or write skew. Use atomic updates, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, a version column or a constraint, or run at serializable and retry the transactions it aborts.
explanation:
The SQL Transactions lesson covered what a transaction promises. This one covers what happens when many run at once. Weaker isolation levels are faster, and each lets a specific, named anomaly through; the bugs they cause appear only under concurrent load, which is why they reach production.

The simulator races two sessions step by step under each level, following how PostgreSQL and MySQL actually behave, including where the two differ.
